Web Development Rules

Web Development Rules

Comprehensive web development rules covering TypeScript, Astro.js, and modern web application patterns

Introduction

Section titled “Introduction”

The Web Development Rules provide comprehensive guidance for building modern, performant web applications using TypeScript and Astro.js, with emphasis on type safety, performance optimization, and developer experience. These rules ensure scalable, maintainable web applications with optimal performance and modern development practices.

Note

Rule Interdependencies: Many rules reference and build upon other rules to ensure consistent code generation.

For example, ASP.NET Core rules automatically incorporate C# coding style guidelines, so all generated API code follows the same performance patterns, memory management, and modern language features.

This creates a cohesive development experience where all code maintains consistent quality and style across different technologies.

Available Rules

Section titled “Available Rules”
TypeScript Coding Style Rules Clean, maintainable TypeScript code with type safety, functional programming patterns, and modern JavaScript features
Astro.js Coding Style Rules Fast, modern websites with Astro's island architecture, static generation, and multi-framework support

TypeScript Coding Style Rules

Section titled “TypeScript Coding Style Rules”

The TypeScript Coding Style Rules establish modern TypeScript development standards with emphasis on type safety, performance optimization, and maintainable code patterns for web applications and libraries.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule provides guidance for:

  • Modern TypeScript capabilities with strict mode configuration
  • Advanced types including utility types, conditional types, and template literal types
  • Comprehensive TypeScript compiler options for maximum safety
  • Generic patterns with constraints and inference
  • Type-safe error handling with Result types
  • Memory-efficient patterns and async optimizations
  • Tree shaking and bundle optimization strategies
  • ESLint configuration with TypeScript-specific checks
  • Framework integration with React, Vue 3, and Node.js

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”

Documentation-Specific Rule

This rule is specifically designed for documentation projects and only applies to files within the docs/ directory.

  • docs/**/*.ts and docs/**/*.css TypeScript and styling files in documentation projects
  • docs/**/*.scss Sass styling files for documentation
  • Files matching the pattern "docs/**/*.js", "docs/**/*.ts", "docs/**/*.md", "docs/**/*.mdx", "docs/**/*.css", "docs/**/*.astro"

Astro.js Coding Style Rules

Section titled “Astro.js Coding Style Rules”

The Astro.js Coding Style Rules provide comprehensive guidance for building fast, modern websites using Astro’s island architecture, static generation, and multi-framework support for optimal performance and developer experience.

What It Does

Section titled “What It Does”

This rule establishes:

  • Build-time optimization for maximum performance
  • Content collections with type-safe content management
  • Automatic image processing and format conversion
  • Multi-framework support (React, Vue, Svelte, Solid.js)
  • Island architecture with selective hydration
  • Type-safe component interfaces and flexible slot patterns
  • Partial hydration with client-side JavaScript only where needed
  • Automatic lazy loading and intelligent prefetching
  • SEO optimization with proper meta tags and Schema.org integration
  • Markdown and MDX support with content collection patterns

File Patterns

Section titled “File Patterns”

Documentation-Specific Rule

This rule is specifically designed for documentation projects and only applies to files within the docs/ directory.

  • docs/**/*.astro component files in documentation projects
  • docs/**/*.js, docs/**/*.ts, docs/**/*.md, docs/**/*.mdx content and configuration files
  • docs/**/*.css and styling files for documentation
  • docs/astro.config.mjs configuration files
